site.title: Skool
site.short_description: Creator communities. Add a profile URL or link in public group posts when rules allow it.
site.long_description: Skool hosts paid and free groups. Owners set link rules. Public post pages often omit nofollow on outbound anchors in page HTML. Profile and social links usually use nofollow. Open the live URL and check rel before you treat a link as a ranking backlink.

opportunities.title: Profile bio link
opportunities.description: Add your site on your Skool profile. Profile and social outbound links use rel=nofollow on live pages. Use this path for clicks and brand, not pass-through DR.

steps.title: Sign in
steps.body: Open Skool and sign in.

steps.title: Open profile
steps.body: Open your profile or account settings from the menu.

steps.title: Add your URL
steps.body: Paste your site into the website or bio field.

steps.title: Save
steps.body: Save and open your public profile. Confirm the link works.

opportunities.title: Group feed post
opportunities.approval_time_hint: Depends on the group owner
opportunities.description: Publish in a public Skool group when rules allow links. Public post permalinks often render body links without nofollow. Owners can remove promo. Schedule on OpenQuok after you connect Skool.

steps.title: Connect Skool
steps.body: Install the OpenQuok extension, stay signed in on Skool, and add the Skool channel. See Skool setup if you need the walkthrough.

steps.title: Pick the group
steps.body: Choose a public group that fits your topic. Read pinned rules for links.

steps.title: Write the post
steps.body: Add title, category label if required, and one URL in the body.

steps.title: Publish or schedule
steps.body: Publish with OpenQuok or schedule for your audience.

steps.title: Check rel
steps.body: Open the public post URL. Inspect your link in page HTML. If rel has nofollow, treat it as nofollow.

site.title: TinyLaunch
site.short_description: Startup launch platform with free Standard queue slots and paid Premium launches.
site.long_description: TinyLaunch lists startups with name, tagline, logo, and category. Makers create a startup profile, then schedule a free Monday Standard slot or pay for Premium placement. OpenQuok can autofill the create-startup form; you choose the queue on TinyLaunch pricing and complete payment on TinyLaunch.

opportunities.title: Premium launch
opportunities.approval_time_hint: Usually within a few business days after you schedule
opportunities.cost_note: $39 per launch on TinyLaunch pricing — see TinyLaunch pricing.
opportunities.description: Premium launch ($39 on TinyLaunch pricing) schedules your startup on TinyLaunch after you create the listing. Confirm link treatment on your live startup page after publish.

steps.title: Review pricing
steps.body: Compare Premium with the free Standard queue on TinyLaunch pricing.

steps.title: Create startup
steps.body: Sign in and complete the create-startup form at TinyLaunch.

steps.title: Schedule Premium
steps.body: Pick a Premium slot and complete checkout. Confirm your live listing when TinyLaunch publishes it.

opportunities.title: Standard launch
opportunities.approval_time_hint: Free Monday slots; timing varies by queue volume
opportunities.description: Join the free Standard queue from TinyLaunch pricing, create your startup profile, then claim the next available Monday slot.

steps.title: Open pricing
steps.body: Review Standard (free) vs Premium on TinyLaunch pricing.

steps.title: Create startup
steps.body: Sign in and fill the shared create-startup form.

steps.title: Schedule Standard
steps.body: Reserve a free Monday slot when the queue allows. Open your live startup URL after publish.

site.title: Chrome Web Store
site.short_description: List a Chrome extension on the Web Store. Point Official URL, homepage, and privacy fields at your site to earn backlinks on the live listing page.
site.long_description: The store runs on google.com. Complete Store listing Additional fields and Privacy before you submit. After approval, open your public listing and confirm each outbound link and rel. Live example: sample Chrome Web Store listing.

opportunities.title: Official URL
opportunities.approval_time_hint: After you submit the listing
opportunities.cost_note: One-time Chrome Web Store developer fee
opportunities.description: Set Additional fields → Official URL to your root domain (your marketing site or company homepage). Do not paste your store listing URL into this field. After approval, check the link on your live store page (see sample Chrome Web Store listing) and confirm rel.

steps.title: Open Developer Dashboard
steps.body: Sign in at Chrome Web Store Dev Console and open your extension under Build.

steps.title: Set Official URL
steps.body: Under Additional fields, verify your domain if Google asks. Enter your root site URL on your own domain.

steps.title: Publish and verify
steps.body: Finish Store listing and Privacy, then submit. Open your public listing (for example sample Chrome Web Store listing) and confirm the official-site link and rel.

opportunities.title: Homepage URL
opportunities.approval_time_hint: Same review as your extension package
opportunities.cost_note: One-time Chrome Web Store developer fee
opportunities.description: Homepage URL in Store listing → Additional fields links buyers to a page on your own domain (your product landing or install page). Do not point this field at your Chrome Web Store listing. After approval, confirm on your live page (see sample Chrome Web Store listing).

steps.title: Open Store listing
steps.body: In the dashboard, go to Build → Store listing.

steps.title: Set Homepage URL
steps.body: In Additional fields, paste your landing or install page. Add Support URL if install docs live on another page.

steps.title: Check the live page
steps.body: After approval, open your public listing (for example sample Chrome Web Store listing) and confirm homepage and support links.

opportunities.title: Privacy policy URL
opportunities.approval_time_hint: Required when the extension uses user data
opportunities.description: Set Build → Privacy to your public privacy policy URL on your own domain. The store page can link out. Match the policy text to your declared permissions.

steps.title: Open Privacy
steps.body: In the dashboard, go to Build → Privacy.

steps.title: Add policy URL
steps.body: Paste your public privacy policy URL on your domain.

steps.title: Confirm on the listing
steps.body: After the listing is live, open your store page (for example sample Chrome Web Store listing) and confirm the privacy link works.

site.title: Microsoft Edge Add-ons
site.short_description: Publish an extension on Edge Add-ons through Partner Center. Set Website and Support contact on Properties. Set Privacy Policy URL on Privacy.
site.long_description: You submit extensions at Partner Center in the Edge workspace. Upload the zip package, then complete Availability, Properties, Privacy, Store listings, and Publish. Certification can take up to seven business days; there is no separate Edge Add-ons listing fee. After the listing is in the store, confirm each outbound link and rel on your live page. Live example: sample Edge Add-ons listing.

opportunities.title: Website
opportunities.approval_time_hint: After certification, usually within seven business days
opportunities.description: On the Properties page, set Website to a page on your own domain (your homepage or product landing). Do not paste your Edge Add-ons listing URL into this field. Users see this link on your live store page after certification (see sample Edge Add-ons listing).

steps.title: Open Partner Center
steps.body: Sign in at Partner Center. Open the Edge workspace and select your extension, or create a new extension and upload your zip package. See Microsoft Edge publish guide for the full flow.

steps.title: Open Properties
steps.body: On the left, click Properties. In Website, enter a page on your site (homepage or product landing). Do not use your listing URL (for example sample Edge Add-ons listing).

steps.title: Publish and verify
steps.body: Click Save & Continue. Complete Privacy and Store listings, then click Publish on the Submit your extension page. When status is In the Store, open your listing (for example sample Edge Add-ons listing) and confirm the Website link.

opportunities.title: Support contact URL
opportunities.approval_time_hint: Same certification pass as your extension package
opportunities.description: On Properties, Support contact detail can be a support page URL or an email. Use a https URL on your domain for a backlink (install docs or help center). Registration values can also show on the store page.

steps.title: Open Properties
steps.body: In Partner Center, open your extension. On the left, click Properties.

steps.title: Set Support contact detail
steps.body: In Support contact detail, paste a support page URL on your domain. You can use an email instead, but email does not give a backlink.

steps.title: Check the live listing
steps.body: Click Save & Continue and finish the remaining Partner Center sections. After certification, open your listing (for example sample Edge Add-ons listing) and confirm the support link.

opportunities.title: Privacy policy URL
opportunities.approval_time_hint: Required when the extension collects user data
opportunities.description: On the Privacy page, set Privacy Policy URL to your public privacy policy on your own domain. The URL must work. Policy text must match the Data usage checkboxes and your extension behavior.

steps.title: Open Privacy
steps.body: In Partner Center, open your extension. On the left, click Privacy.

steps.title: Complete privacy sections
steps.body: Fill Single purpose, Permission justification, and Data usage. These fields must match your manifest and your policy.

steps.title: Set Privacy Policy URL
steps.body: In Privacy Policy URL, paste your public privacy policy URL. Click Save & Continue, finish Store listings, and Publish.

steps.title: Confirm on the listing
steps.body: After the extension is In the Store, open your listing (for example sample Edge Add-ons listing) and confirm the privacy link loads.

site.title: Firefox Add-ons (AMO)
site.short_description: Publish a Firefox add-on on addons.mozilla.org (AMO). Set Homepage and Support site on the developer hub. Add links in About this extension. Add a privacy policy when you collect user data.
site.long_description: Submit a signed build through the Firefox Add-ons developer hub. AMO review can take days. Homepage and Support site appear under Add-on Links. You can also paste https links to your own domain in About this extension — Mozilla routes them through outgoing and usually marks them nofollow. Check rel on your live listing. Live example: sample AMO listing.

opportunities.title: Homepage
opportunities.approval_time_hint: After AMO approves the listing
opportunities.description: On the AMO listing edit page, set Homepage to a page on your own domain (homepage or product landing). Do not paste your AMO listing URL into this field. It appears under Add-on Links on the public page. Verify rel on your live listing (see sample AMO listing).

steps.title: Open the developer hub
steps.body: Sign in to Firefox Add-ons. Open your add-on in the developer hub.

steps.title: Set Homepage
steps.body: In Edit, set Homepage to your product landing or marketing site on your domain.

steps.title: Publish and verify
steps.body: Submit a new version or update metadata and wait for review. Open your public listing (for example sample AMO listing) and confirm the Homepage link and rel.

opportunities.title: About description links
opportunities.approval_time_hint: Same AMO review as your add-on package
opportunities.description: The About this extension body on AMO supports rich text and markdown. Add https links to pages on your own domain (not your AMO listing URL). Mozilla wraps external URLs through outgoing and usually sets rel="nofollow". Verify href and rel on your live listing (see sample AMO listing).

steps.title: Open listing edit
steps.body: In the AMO developer hub, open your add-on and go to Edit.

steps.title: Edit About this extension
steps.body: In the description or summary field, add markdown links or bare https URLs to pages on your own domain.

steps.title: Publish and verify rel
steps.body: Submit a new version or update metadata and wait for review. Open your public listing (for example sample AMO listing). In About this extension, confirm each link href and rel.

opportunities.title: Support site
opportunities.approval_time_hint: Same AMO review as your add-on package
opportunities.description: Set Support site in the developer hub to a https page on your own domain (install docs or help center). Support email alone does not give a URL backlink. Confirm under Add-on Links on your live listing (see sample AMO listing).

steps.title: Open listing edit
steps.body: In the AMO developer hub, open your add-on and go to Edit.

steps.title: Set Support site
steps.body: Enter Support site URL on your domain.

steps.title: Check Add-on Links
steps.body: After approval, open your public listing (for example sample AMO listing). Under Add-on Links, confirm Support site href and rel.

opportunities.title: Privacy policy
opportunities.approval_time_hint: Required when the add-on collects user data
opportunities.description: AMO shows Read the privacy policy when you declare data collection. Host the policy on your own domain. Match the text to permission and data declarations in the add-on submission.

steps.title: Open privacy fields
steps.body: In the developer hub, open your add-on version or Edit. Open the privacy and data collection sections.

steps.title: Set policy URL
steps.body: Enter your public privacy policy URL and complete data-collection disclosures.

steps.title: Confirm on AMO
steps.body: After approval, open your public listing (for example sample AMO listing). Confirm the privacy policy link under More information.

site.title: Fazier
site.short_description: Product launch and company pages for startups. OpenQuok fills the forms. You sign in and finish badges, comments, or payment on Fazier.
site.long_description: Fazier publishes launches and company pages. Launch pages link to your website. The free Basic plan asks for a Fazier badge or a link to Fazier on your site. Paid plans offer stronger backlink promises. See plans on Fazier submit. OpenQuok fills the forms. You approve and submit on Fazier.

opportunities.title: Page
opportunities.approval_time_hint: Usually within a few business days after you submit
opportunities.description: OpenQuok fills the Fazier company form. Add your name, website, and company story. Launch pages are the main path for links to your site. Check your live page after Fazier approves it.

steps.title: Sign in
steps.body: Open Fazier and sign in with Google or email.

steps.title: Basic info
steps.body: Open Fazier company form. In step 1, add company name, page address, website, logo, and tagline.

steps.title: Overview and socials
steps.body: Add industry, size, type, country, city, founded date, about text, and social links. Fill any extra fields Fazier shows.

steps.title: Publish and verify
steps.body: Submit the page. Open your live company page. Check any link to your website. Launches use separate rules on Fazier submit.

opportunities.title: Free product listing
opportunities.approval_time_hint: Basic tier: reviewed within about 30 days
opportunities.cost_note: Add a Fazier badge or a link to Fazier on your site.
opportunities.description: OpenQuok fills the product form at Fazier submit. Choose the free Basic plan. Add the badge or site link Fazier asks for. Launch pages usually link to your product site.

steps.title: Pick Basic (free)
steps.body: Compare tiers on Fazier launch tiers, then open Fazier submit and choose Product launch and the Basic plan.

steps.title: Fill and review
steps.body: Use the OpenQuok extension to fill the form. Check each field before you submit on Fazier.

steps.title: Finish manual requirements
steps.body: Leave maker comments, add the Fazier embed badge or homepage/footer link, and wait for approval.

steps.title: Save your listing
steps.body: When Fazier publishes, open your launch page. Save your live listing URL.

opportunities.title: Paid product listing
opportunities.approval_time_hint: Lite Plan and higher can publish or schedule sooner
opportunities.cost_note: Lite about $29. Premium about $49. Super about $99. Fazier lists a different backlink promise for each tier.
opportunities.description: OpenQuok fills the product form at Fazier submit. Choose Lite, Premium, or Super. You do not need the free Basic badge or site link. Read each tier on Fazier before you pay.

steps.title: Pick a paid tier
steps.body: Compare Lite, Premium, and Super on Fazier launch tiers, then open Fazier submit and choose Product launch with your paid plan.

steps.title: Fill and review
steps.body: Use the OpenQuok extension to fill the form. Check each field before you continue on Fazier.

steps.title: Checkout on Fazier
steps.body: Pay on Fazier. Paid plans do not need the free Basic badge or homepage link.

steps.title: Save your listing
steps.body: When Fazier publishes, open your launch page. Save your live listing URL. Check the link matches the tier you bought.

site.title: DevHunt
site.short_description: Launch platform for developer tools. Free listing with a permanent page, or a $49 launch week for a dofollow link. No badge required.
site.long_description: DevHunt lists developer tools on launch days. See devhunt.org and the submit flow before you pay for a launch week.

opportunities.title: Free listing
opportunities.approval_time_hint: Permanent tool page after DevHunt publishes
opportunities.cost_note: Free listing links use nofollow. No DevHunt badge is required on your site.
opportunities.description: List a developer tool on DevHunt at no cost. You get a permanent tool page with a nofollow link to your site. OpenQuok fills new tool form after you sign in.

steps.title: Confirm developer focus
steps.body: Use this path only for developer tools. DevHunt removes consumer apps and general marketing tools.

steps.title: Read the launch guide
steps.body: Review listing vs launch rules on DevHunt.

steps.title: Sign in
steps.body: Open DevHunt sign in and sign in with GitHub, Google, or email.

steps.title: Submit your tool
steps.body: Open new tool form. Use OpenQuok to fill name, slogan, website, description, logo (about 220 by 220 pixels), and at least three screenshots. Put your product in the first screenshot. Submit the free listing on DevHunt.

steps.title: Verify after publish
steps.body: When DevHunt publishes your tool, open the live page. Confirm the website link works. Save your live listing URL.

opportunities.title: Paid launch
opportunities.approval_time_hint: You pick the launch week after $49 checkout on DevHunt
opportunities.cost_note: $49 one-time launch week on DevHunt: dofollow link, homepage spot, and newsletter slot.
opportunities.description: Pay $49 on DevHunt for a launch week. You choose the week and get a permanent dofollow link, homepage placement, and newsletter exposure. OpenQuok fills the form first. Checkout and launch week stay on DevHunt.

steps.title: Confirm developer focus
steps.body: Use this path only for developer tools. DevHunt removes consumer apps and general marketing tools.

steps.title: Compare listing and launch
steps.body: Read what the $49 launch includes vs a free listing on DevHunt.

steps.title: Sign in and open the form
steps.body: Sign in at DevHunt sign in. Open new tool form.

steps.title: Fill and submit
steps.body: Use OpenQuok to complete the tool form. Add logo (about 220 by 220 pixels) and at least three screenshots. Submit on DevHunt.

steps.title: Pay and pick launch week
steps.body: On DevHunt, pay $49 and pick your launch week. After publish, open your live tool page and confirm the dofollow website link. Save your live listing URL.

site.title: Nick Launches
site.short_description: Product launch directory with a free listing path and paid featured launches. OpenQuok fills the submit form; you verify the badge, pick a plan, and finish review on Nick Launches.
site.long_description: Nick Launches lists products with taglines, media, and categories. Free listings need weekly upvotes and a live Featured badge on your site for a dofollow link. Paid tiers ($19, $39, $99, or $199 one-time) skip the badge requirement and include a featured window — choose the plan on Nick Launches submit plan after the listing form. All submissions go through admin review.

opportunities.title: Free launch
opportunities.approval_time_hint: Admin review after you submit; dofollow needs weekly upvotes plus a live Featured badge
opportunities.cost_note: Free listing is $0. Add the live Featured badge from nicklaunches.com/badge/ on your site for dofollow; earn weekly upvotes to stay featured.
opportunities.description: List your product at no cost on Nick Launches submit. OpenQuok fills the listing form after you sign in. Finish on Nick Launches: pick the free path on submit plan, add the Featured badge for dofollow, and wait for admin approval.

steps.title: Read launch rules
steps.body: Review free vs paid paths on Nick Launches. Free listings need the Featured badge on your site and ongoing weekly upvotes for dofollow.

steps.title: Sign in
steps.body: Open Nick Launches sign in and sign in. Skip or review any website URL prefill before OpenQuok fills the form.

steps.title: Submit listing
steps.body: Open Nick Launches submit. Use OpenQuok to fill name, tagline, description, logo, screenshots, categories, and links. Submit the listing on Nick Launches.

steps.title: Pick free plan and badge
steps.body: On submit plan, choose the free option. Install the live Featured badge on your product site. Earn weekly upvotes after Nick Launches approves the listing.

steps.title: Verify after publish
steps.body: When Nick Launches publishes your product, open the live page. Confirm the website link and rel match the free-tier rules. Save your live listing URL.

opportunities.title: Paid launch
opportunities.approval_time_hint: Admin review after checkout; featured window starts after Nick Launches approves
opportunities.cost_note: One-time tiers on submit plan: $19, $39, $99, or $199. Paid plans make the Featured badge optional and include a featured launch window.
opportunities.description: OpenQuok fills Nick Launches submit after you sign in. Pay on submit plan ($19, $39, $99, or $199 one-time). Paid tiers skip the badge requirement and add a featured window — checkout and launch timing stay on Nick Launches.

steps.title: Compare free and paid
steps.body: Read what paid tiers include vs the free badge path on Nick Launches before you checkout.

steps.title: Sign in and open the form
steps.body: Sign in at Nick Launches sign in. Open submit new. Skip or review URL prefill before OpenQuok fills fields.

steps.title: Fill and submit listing
steps.body: Use OpenQuok to complete the product form. Submit the listing on Nick Launches.

steps.title: Pay and pick plan
steps.body: On submit plan, choose a paid tier and complete checkout ($19, $39, $99, or $199). The Featured badge is optional on paid plans.

steps.title: Verify after publish
steps.body: After admin approval, open your live product page. Confirm the dofollow website link and featured placement. Save your live listing URL.

opportunities.title: Maker profile
opportunities.approval_time_hint: Usually within a few business days after you save your profile
opportunities.description: Create a maker profile with your website and social links at no cost. OpenQuok fills Nick Launches profile after you sign in. Confirm link treatment on your public profile URL after Nick Launches publishes it.

steps.title: Sign in
steps.body: Open Nick Launches sign in and sign in.

steps.title: Open profile
steps.body: Go to Nick Launches profile. Use OpenQuok to fill headline, bio, website, avatar, and social links where shown.

steps.title: Save and verify
steps.body: Save your profile on Nick Launches. Open your public profile URL, inspect the website link rel, and save the live profile link.

site.title: Uneed
site.short_description: Launch directory with paid product features and a free maker profile.
site.long_description: Uneed offers paid launches and a free maker profile. Review pricing at uneed.best/pricing.

opportunities.title: Free launch (join the line)
opportunities.description: Launch a new product on the free Join the line tier at Uneed pricing ($0). Uneed picks your launch date (at most about five months out). You need an upvote score of 10 for the listing to stay live and 20 for a dofollow backlink from their 75 DR domain—confirm rel on your live product page after launch day.

steps.body: On Pricing, open Launch → New product → Join the line and note upvote thresholds (10 to stay published, 20 for dofollow) and how the queue assigns dates.
steps.title: Read free launch rules

steps.body: Submit your product on Uneed with accurate URL and assets. Promote launch day to reach score 20 if you want the dofollow backlink—inspect the listing link after you go live.
steps.title: Submit and earn upvotes

opportunities.title: Paid launch listing
opportunities.approval_time_hint: Usually within a few business days
opportunities.description: Featured launch placement with a prominent product link. Third-party launch directories usually link to your site without nofollow on listing pages — confirm on the live Uneed product card.

opportunities.title: Free maker profile
opportunities.description: Create a profile with your project URL at no cost. Maker profiles on Uneed typically use nofollow listing links; verify rel on your public profile URL.

steps.body: Sign up at uneed.best, open your maker profile, and add your product name plus homepage URL in the website field.
steps.title: Create your maker profile

steps.body: Open your public profile (for example uneed.best/profile/your-handle), right-click the website link → Inspect, and confirm rel includes nofollow. Re-check after Uneed updates—launch listings use different rules than profiles.
steps.title: Confirm link treatment

site.title: GitHub
site.short_description: Profiles, project sites, and package pages on github.com — each surface has different link rules.
site.long_description: GitHub offers profile README, Pages, and container package pages. README links on github.com use nofollow. Pages links follow your HTML. See GitHub Pages docs.

opportunities.title: Profile README
opportunities.description: Create a public repository named like your username with a README.md — GitHub renders it on your profile. README and profile website links on github.com are nofollow.

steps.body: New repository named exactly your GitHub username (e.g. octocat/octocat), public, with a README.
steps.title: Create the profile repo

steps.body: Introduce yourself or your product and include one clear link to your marketing site or docs.
steps.title: Write the README

steps.body: Profile → Edit profile → Website — paste the same primary URL for visitors who skip the README.
steps.title: Set profile website

opportunities.title: GitHub Pages site
opportunities.description: Publish a static site or docs on github.io (or a custom domain). Unlike READMEs on github.com, Pages serves your HTML without adding rel=nofollow to outbound links you author.

steps.body: Repository Settings → Pages — deploy from a branch or GitHub Actions workflow.
steps.title: Choose Pages source

steps.body: Add HTML or Markdown with contextual copy; place your canonical product URL in header, footer, or About page.
steps.title: Publish content

steps.body: Inspect a live outbound link on your Pages URL — it should not include nofollow unless you added it in your template or markup.
steps.title: Verify rel attributes

opportunities.title: Profile website and social links
opportunities.description: Edit your public GitHub profile and add your primary site in Website, plus up to four Social accounts (LinkedIn, X, or other URLs). See adding social links to your profile; links on github.com are typically nofollow but strong for discovery.

steps.body: From your profile, choose Edit profile, or open Public profile settings.
steps.title: Open profile settings — From your profile, choose Edit profile, or go to Settings → Public profile.

steps.body: Paste your marketing site in Website; fill Social accounts with relevant links (company, docs, LinkedIn, X) — then Save.
steps.title: Add Website and social URLs

opportunities.title: Container package (GHCR)
opportunities.description: Publish an OCI image to GitHub Container Registry under your user or org. The package page lives on github.com — README and repo links use GitHub’s nofollow sanitizer, similar to profile READMEs.

steps.body: Push a tagged image to ghcr.io with a workflow or docker push; link the package to the source repository.
steps.title: Publish the image

steps.body: Add description and source-repo metadata; treat external links as discovery for people, not dofollow SEO from github.com.
steps.title: Set package metadata

steps.body: In the repo README, link the GHCR pull command and your primary site — expect nofollow on github.com-rendered anchors.
steps.title: Surface install docs

site.title: Threads
site.short_description: Text-first social posts from Meta — profiles and threads for brand
site.long_description: Threads profiles can include one website link. Confirm rel on your public profile. Open threads.net.

opportunities.title: Personal profile link
opportunities.description: Use your main personal Threads profile—the one tied to your day-to-day Instagram login—and add your site in bio or profile fields. Good for founders who want one handle for you and your project.

steps.body: Open Threads with the personal Instagram-linked account you use as yourself, then open profile settings.
steps.title: Open your personal profile

steps.body: Paste your URL in the profile link or bio field Meta provides, save, and confirm on your public profile.
steps.title: Add your link

opportunities.title: Thread post with link
opportunities.description: After your profile lists your site, publish a Threads post with your URL. Post on Threads or schedule in OpenQuok once your channel is connected.

steps.body: Write a short update and include your URL once with context.
steps.title: Compose your post

steps.body: Post now or schedule in OpenQuok for Threads alongside your other channels.
steps.title: Publish or schedule

opportunities.title: Reply with link
opportunities.description: Reply on Threads with a reply and your URL when it fits. On threads you publish, OpenQuok Auto plug post automate a follow-up with your link after likes or on your schedule. Set up plugs after you connect Threads.

steps.body: On Threads, join a relevant conversation, add a useful reply, and include your URL once when it fits the thread.
steps.title: Reply with a link

steps.body: On threads you publish, connect Threads in OpenQuok and attach plug (like threshold + reply with your link). OpenQuok publishes the follow-up when your rules match so you do not have to bump the thread yourself.
steps.title: a follow-up on your threads

site.title: Tiktok
site.short_description: Short-form video — bio link for mobile-first audiences.
site.long_description: TikTok profiles can include a website field when eligible. Confirm rel on your public profile. See tiktok.com.

opportunities.title: Personal profile website link
opportunities.description: Add your site to the website field on your personal TikTok profile once you have at least 1,000 followers. Use the account you post from as yourself.
